node-1.label: Initial gastroscopic examination revealed lesions in the gastric antrum

node-2.label: A 52-year-old male presented on July 10, 2019 with an unremarkable past medical history

node-3.label: The patient underwent laparoscopy-assisted distal gastrectomy and Billroth II gastrojejunostomy on July 23, 2019, followed by eight cycles of adjuvant chemotherapy with SOX regimen (oxaliplatin + tegafur, gimeracil and oteracil potassium) and 25 doses of radiotherapy in May 2020

node-4.label: During treatment, the patient experienced grade II neutrophils, grade I nausea, grade I neurotoxicity, grade II diarrhea with weight loss, rash, pruritus, and grade II oral ulcer

why.why: Postoperative pathology is the gold standard for tumor diagnosis and definitively confirms poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma (diffuse type) with serosal/pancreatic invasion, vascular tumor thrombus, perineural invasion, duodenal involvement, and 8/51 positive lymph nodes (pT4bN3a). The molecular findings of HER2 2+ with ~10% amplification and intact MMR proteins further support the malignant nature and guide targeted therapy. Therefore, confidence in gastric malignant tumor is raised from 0.9 to 0.99.

The pathological confirmation of adenocarcinoma with invasive features, lymph node metastases, and perineural/vascular invasion definitively excludes a benign gastric ulcer or polyp. The radical surgery and oncologic treatment already argued against benign disease; the pathology findings now provide conclusive refutation, lowering confidence to 0.01.

node-8.label: Molecular testing showed HER2 2+ with HER2 amplification in approximately 10% of tumor cells and intact MMR protein expression
